title: NetOps Safety Testbed v1 — Integrated Generation→Verify→Emulate Benchmark (Preregistration)
research_question: Can a compact, public NetOps safety testbed combining intent-to-config generation, grammar-constrained decoding, formal verification, and emulation-execution metrics provide reproducible baseline measurements and expose recurrent failure modes of LLM-driven NetOps pipelines?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Constrained-decoding + verifier gating reduces the per-intent unsafe-change rate (absolute) by ≥10 percentage points compared with single-shot prompting (paired estimand).

H2: Iterative verifier-guided repair decreases residual unsafe-change rate relative to single-shot generation, but with diminishing returns after K=2 repair iterations; recurrent failure patterns will concentrate in a small set of categories (vendor-syntax, missing state, policy-violation).
exploratory_questions: E1: Which failure categories dominate across vendor clusters and prompting methods?
E2: How often do verifier false negatives (unsafe change accepted) occur compared with emulator-observed unsafe outcomes?
E3: What is the distribution of model-call cost vs. residual unsafe rate for the iterative repair method (cost-effectiveness frontier)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic, sanitized, multi-vendor intent set (abstracted CLI templates for four vendor-clusters: vendorA, vendorB, vendorC, vendorD).
End-to-end pipeline: generation → grammar/LMQL constraint → formal verifier (reachability + policy) → Mininet emulation execution → automatic rollback-cost metric.
Public artifacts limited to synthetic, redacted, template-based command sequences and machine-readable evaluation scripts (no real customer data).
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API endpoint available under the run capability.
Three prompting strategies applied to the hosted LLM: (1) single-shot baseline, (2) constrained-decoding (grammar/LMQL wrapper), (3) iterative verifier-guided repair (bound K=2).
transformation_scope: Intent → reference-config mapping via deterministic template expansion (synthetic state parameters).
Grammar-constrained decoding (LMQL-like) to enforce CLI token-level schema.
Automatic sanitizer transforming any detected sensitive tokens into abstract placeholders during dataset generation and output sanitization.
primary_estimand: Paired per-intent difference in unsafe-change indicator (unsafe after emulation execution) between constrained-decoding (method 2) and single-shot baseline (method 1).
secondary_estimands: Per-method residual unsafe rate after verifier gating (proportion of emulation runs producing unsafe outcome).
Average model-calls per successful safe configuration (cost-effectiveness).
Distribution (frequency) of failure categories across vendor clusters.
sampling_plan: Total 240 synthetic intents: 200 confirmatory intents (50 per vendor-cluster) + 40 exploratory/adversarial intents. For each intent, run three methods (methods 1–3). Per-intent per-method replicates: 3 seeded stochastic generations. Iterative method (method 3) allowed up to K=2 repair iterations; per-replicate model-call usage recorded. All intents and RNG seeds recorded; synthetic templates sanitized to remove any identifying tokens. Flagged/public-release exclusions deterministically replaced from the same template seed pool to preserve confirmatory n=200.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand power target: detect absolute paired reduction Δ=0.10 with α=0.05, power≈0.8. Assumptions: baseline single-shot unsafe≈20%; paired n=200 confirmatory intents chosen based on conservative paired/paired-equivalent approximation (sample-size calc ≈196). Per-intent replicates collapsed via logical OR to a single per-method unsafe indicator. Sensitivity analyses: recompute CIs under baseline rates 15% and 25%; per-cluster exploratory estimates reported with wider CIs. Nonconvergent iterative runs counted as unsafe (conservative) and alternate available-pair sensitivity reported.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any synthetic intent or generated output that fails the sanitization regex checks (IP, domain, email, credential-like patterns) from public release; deterministic replacement intent drawn to maintain confirmatory sample size.
Exclude any generated config that fails grammar parse or contains unresolved redaction placeholders from public artifact set; include such replicates in internal logs only for diagnostic analysis.

If a replicate suffers infrastructure/API technical failure (API error, timeout) the replicate is marked technical-failure and excluded from primary paired analysis as specified in missingness_plan; counts and reasons published.
missingness_plan: Model/API errors or timeouts recorded as 'technical failure' and excluded from primary confirmatory analysis; counts and causes published. For iterative-method runs aborted by infrastructure failure, the affected per-intent replicate is marked missing and the entire intent replicate excluded from paired primary analysis; publish sensitivity analysis using available-pair approach. No human imputation or manual annotation. All exclusions and replacements are deterministic and logged with hashes.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: per-intent paired comparison (method2 vs method1) of binary unsafe indicator (emulation result) using McNemar's test (two-sided, α=0.05); report exact p-value and 95% CI for paired risk difference. Collapse 3 replicates per intent by logical OR to form per-method unsafe indicator; nonconvergent iterative runs counted as unsafe in primary analysis. Secondary analyses: per-method residual unsafe rates with binomial CIs, model-calls per safe outcome and cost-effectiveness frontier, contingency tables of failure categories by vendor cluster, descriptive verifier FP/FN rates (verifier vs emulation). All analyses computed deterministically by published code; exploratory tests reported unadjusted and labeled exploratory. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses per power_plan are executed and reported.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is the single pre-specified paired comparison (controls multiplicity for main claim). Secondary and exploratory analyses are labeled exploratory; unadjusted p-values reported. When multiple secondary comparisons are presented, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values provided in published auxiliary artifacts (appendix).

stopping_rule: Stop conditions (apply during execution): (1) stop the run if cumulative model calls reach the planned model-call budget for the selected scenario plus 5% buffer (recommended_full planned_model_calls=2880 → hard stop at 3024 calls). (2) stop and abort confirmatory run if infrastructure/API outage prevents progress for >24 continuous hours; record as technical failure and report. (3) stop early and switch to contingency minimal scenario if >15% of confirmatory intents require deterministic replacement due to contamination/sanitization (indicates template pool insufficiency); document and publish rationale and replacement protocol. (4) safety stop: if any generated config produces an emulator-observed outcome outside the defined emulation safety envelope that could indicate emulator or verifier bug (not intended in synthetic scope), pause and investigate before proceeding; document any deviation.
